task.description: Step 01: root cause diagnosis for TC-ISS-203-02 QueryFailed on ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING replay insert.

test_refs.test_name: TC-ISS-203-02: replay dedup — ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING absorbs second insert

result.summary: Root cause confirmed: Schema mismatch (root-cause class A). After PAR-01 partitioning (migration 1147_par01_events_partitioning.sql, shipped in commit 38cb7967), the uq_event_idempotency UNIQUE index on events(idempotency_key) was DELIBERATELY DROPPED — global idempotency-key uniqueness was moved to the new non-partitioned sidecar table plat_event_idempotency (idempotency_key PRIMARY KEY). The test TC-ISS-203-02 (tests/integration/iss203_idempotency_keys_test.zig:367-380) issues INSERT INTO events … ON CONFLICT (idempotency_key) DO NOTHING against the partitioned events table, which now has NO unique index on idempotency_key — PostgreSQL returns SQLSTATE 42P10 'there is no unique or exclusion constraint matching the ON CONFLICT specification', pg.zig surfaces it as PgError.ServerError (vendor/pg/pg.zig:329), pool.zig wraps it as PoolError.QueryFailed (src/db/pool.zig:526). Verified live against tenant_default.events on the test DB at port 5434 (scratch/gh764_oc_test.log, scratch/gh764_tenant_events_idx.log) and reproduced end-to-end via `zig build test-integration-iss203` (scratch/gh764_iss203_run.log). Pre-PAR-01 the test would have passed because uq_event_idempotency existed (migrations/001_event_store.sql:49); the test was written under that schema and was not updated when PAR-01 redesign landed. NOT a production bug: src/event_store/store.zig:291 already uses plat_event_idempotency correctly. NOT category B/C/D/E.
result.root_cause_class: A — Schema mismatch (test design outdated by PAR-01)

evidence.result: FAILED: TC-ISS-203-02 — Unexpected error during replay insert: error.QueryFailed

evidence.command: docker-compose exec -T db_test psql -U bpm -d bpm_test -c "INSERT INTO tenant_default.events (...) ON CONFLICT (idempotency_key) DO NOTHING"
evidence.result: ERROR: there is no unique or exclusion constraint matching the ON CONFLICT specification

evidence.command: SELECT indexname, indexdef FROM pg_indexes WHERE schemaname='tenant_default' AND tablename='events'
evidence.result: 10 indexes, none on idempotency_key. Confirmed absent: uq_event_idempotency. Only events_pkey (event_id, created_at) and uq_event_sequence (instance_id, sequence_number, created_at) provide uniqueness.

evidence.command: SELECT conname, contype, pg_get_constraintdef(oid) FROM pg_constraint WHERE conrelid = 'tenant_default.events'::regclass
evidence.result: Only events_pkey (PRIMARY KEY (event_id, created_at)). No UNIQUE constraint on idempotency_key.

Line 162-164 explicitly notes: 'uq_event_idempotency (idempotency_key) is deliberately NOT recreated here — global idempotency now lives in plat_event_idempotency (Migration 2 below). Partitioning would otherwise silently narrow idempotency_key uniqueness to per-partition scope, which PAR-01 AC2 forbids.' Lines 176-201: plat_event_idempotency table created with idempotency_key PRIMARY KEY.
Last test edit: 3eca5be2 (ISS-203 original commit). PAR-01 migration (38cb7967) is more recent — test was not updated to match.

evidence.snippet: INSERT INTO plat_event_idempotency (idempotency_key, event_id, created_at) VALUES ($1, gen_random_uuid(), NOW()) ON CONFLICT (idempotency_key) DO NOTHING
evidence.significance: Production code already uses plat_event_idempotency correctly. The bug is in the test, not in production.

evidence.snippet: global idempotency-key uniqueness preserved via a new, non-partitioned plat_event_idempotency table written in the same transaction as every append

file_line_citations.original_unique_index: migrations/001_event_store.sql:49 (CREATE UNIQUE INDEX uq_event_idempotency ON events(idempotency_key))
file_line_citations.original_commit: ISS-203 initial commit 3eca5be2 — test predates PAR-01 (38cb7967)

diagnosis_notes: Category E (stale-evidence) is RULED OUT: the live test execution reproduces the failure deterministically against the current production DB. NOT a transient DB state.

Category C (schema-not-migrated) is RULED OUT: tenant_default.events is partitioned (relkind=p) and matches the PAR-01 expected shape; the migration ran correctly. The test's assumption that uq_event_idempotency exists is what is wrong.
Category D (production code bug) is RULED OUT: src/event_store/store.zig:291 uses plat_event_idempotency ON CONFLICT correctly. Production replay dedup works.
Category B (missing requirement) is RULED OUT: the test's intent is valid (verify ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING absorbs replay inserts); it is the implementation that is wrong, not the requirement.

Category A (schema mismatch) is CONFIRMED: the test ON CONFLICT targets idempotency_key on events, but the post-PAR-01 schema has no unique constraint on events(idempotency_key). The intended uniqueness target is plat_event_idempotency (per the migration comment), but the test never migrated its ON CONFLICT target.

Fix direction: the test should target plat_event_idempotency instead of events. Specifically, the ON CONFLICT (idempotency_key) DO NOTHING must be applied to the INSERT INTO plat_event_idempotency (not INSERT INTO events). This matches the production code path at src/event_store/store.zig:288-294. Alternative fix: drop the unique-index-on-events requirement entirely and split into two statements — first INSERT INTO plat_event_idempotency (idempotency_key) VALUES ($1) ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, then INSERT INTO events SELECT … WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM plat_event_idempotency WHERE idempotency_key=$1). The first alternative (single INSERT … SELECT INTO plat_event_idempotency with RETURNING, then INSERT INTO events) more faithfully reproduces the production path.
